faq.question: Is Event Schedule a good Google Forms alternative for events?
faq.answer: Yes. Event Schedule replaces Google Forms for event registration with built-in ticketing, payments, and attendee management. You can set up your first event in minutes. Paste your event details and AI will extract dates, times, and descriptions automatically.

faq.question: Is Event Schedule really free?
faq.answer: Yes. The free plan includes unlimited events, Google Calendar sync, newsletters, and fan engagement features. Selling tickets is free too, up to 25 paid ones a month with zero platform fees and the QR on each scanned at the door; Pro at $5/month removes the cap and adds the live check-in dashboard. Buyers pay through Stripe or PayPal, or by Payfast for rand, Invoice Ninja, a payment link or cash, on every plan. No credit card required to start.

faq.question: Can Event Schedule handle custom registration fields like Google Forms?
faq.answer: Yes. Pro plan includes custom fields on ticket forms so you can collect any information you need from attendees. Unlike Google Forms, the data is automatically connected to your attendee records and ticket sales.

faq.question: Can I replace a notify-me form for an event that is not on sale yet?
faq.answer: Yes, and it is free on every plan. On an event with nothing on sale yet, visitors click Tell me when tickets go on sale and leave just an email address, with no account. They get one email when tickets go on sale, one if the event is cancelled, a reminder shortly before it starts, and any notice you choose to send if the date or venue changes. It does not add them to your newsletter, every email has a one-click unsubscribe, and the event editor shows you how many people are waiting.

faq.question: Can I collect RSVPs for free events without Google Forms?
faq.answer: Yes. Event Schedule supports free RSVPs with automatic confirmation emails and an optional capacity limit, with no payment setup at all. Attendees register through your event page, and you get a real attendee list with a QR code for each guest to scan at the door, not just form responses.

faq.question: Is Event Schedule a good Mailchimp alternative for event emails?
faq.answer: Yes. Event Schedule includes newsletters with A/B testing, segments, list import, and an automatic digest of new events for confirmed subscribers, all beside your ticket sales. You can send event announcements and updates directly from your schedule without a separate email tool.

faq.question: How much does Event Schedule cost compared to Mailchimp?
faq.answer: The newsletter tools and your subscriber list are free, with no cap on how many subscribers you keep. What the plan sets is the monthly newsletter allowance, counted in recipients: 10 on the free plan, 100 on Pro at $5/month and 1,000 on Enterprise, so one newsletter to 40 people uses 40 of it. The automatic digest of new events does not count against it. Selling tickets is free as well, 25 paid ones a month with zero platform fees. Mailchimp charges based on contact count and can cost $20 or more per month for similar email features alone.

faq.question: Does Event Schedule support email automation like Mailchimp?
faq.answer: Some, aimed at events. Confirmed subscribers get a digest of the new public events your schedule creates automatically, at most one every 72 hours, and it does not draw on the newsletter allowance. People who ask to hear about one event get an email when its tickets go on sale, one if it is cancelled, and a reminder shortly before it starts. What it does not have is Mailchimp-style drip sequences or custom automation rules: a newsletter goes out when you send it.

faq.question: Can I import my Mailchimp subscriber list?
faq.answer: Yes. Export your audience from Mailchimp, then paste the addresses in or upload the CSV, up to 10,000 rows at a time, on any plan. They land in a segment you can send newsletters to. From then on, people sign up on your schedule page, and buyers who tick the box at checkout join your subscribers.

faq.question: Can I send newsletters to people who bought tickets?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose the Ticket buyers segment and a newsletter reaches everyone who bought tickets to your events, or to one event you pick, without importing anything. Buyers who ticked the box at checkout to hear from you are on your subscriber list too, and get the automatic digest.

faq.question: Is signing up double opt-in, like Mailchimp?
faq.answer: On the sign-up panel, yes. Visitors give a name and an email address and confirm from the email that follows; confirming also sets up an account that follows your schedule. The tick box at checkout is single opt-in, because the order receipt has already proved the address.

faq.question: Is Event Schedule a good Calendly alternative for public events?
faq.answer: Yes. Calendly is built for one-on-one appointment scheduling. Event Schedule takes those bookings too, free with one appointment type, and is built for public events with audiences. You get public event pages, ticket sales, a shareable schedule, newsletters, and event graphics that Calendly does not offer.

faq.question: Does Event Schedule have a free plan?
faq.answer: Yes. The free plan includes unlimited events, public event pages, one bookable appointment type, Google Calendar sync, newsletters, and fan engagement features. Selling tickets is free too, up to 25 paid ones a month with zero platform fees and the QR on each scanned at the door; Pro at $5/month removes the cap and adds the live check-in dashboard.

faq.question: Does Event Schedule sync with Google Calendar like Calendly?
faq.answer: Yes. Event Schedule includes two-way Google Calendar sync on the free plan. Events you create sync to your Google Calendar, and Google Calendar events can sync back. CalDAV sync is also supported.

faq.question: Can attendees add events to their own Google Calendar?
faq.answer: Yes. Event pages include an option to add the event to Google Calendar or download an iCal file. Guests can also subscribe to a live calendar feed of your schedule, which adds every event and updates itself when dates change. Two-way Google Calendar sync also keeps your own calendar updated automatically when you create or edit events in Event Schedule.

faq.question: Can I use Event Schedule for recurring events?
faq.answer: Yes. Event Schedule supports recurring events with flexible scheduling patterns. Each occurrence can have its own ticket types and attendee limits, which is something Calendly cannot handle for public events.

faq.question: Can people still book a slot with me one to one?
faq.answer: Yes, and that part is free with one appointment type. Publish the hours you are available, set the slot length and the interval between start times, add buffers either side, and people pick a time in their own timezone from a public booking page. Overrides cover the days that are different, an approval step is optional, and a slot can take payment through Stripe, a payment link or cash (PayPal and Payfast are for tickets, not bookings). Nothing can be booked over something already on your schedule, synced calendar entries included. More than one appointment type is on the Pro plan.

faq.question: What happens if somebody needs to move their booking?
faq.answer: They reschedule it themselves from the private link in their confirmation, and you can do it from the booking row. It moves the existing booking rather than cancelling and rebooking, so the payment, the private link and the calendar entry all carry over instead of the guest having to pay again.

faq.question: Can I refund a booking?
faq.answer: Yes, from the Sales page, where bookings sit with your other sales. A booking paid through Stripe can be refunded in full or in part, and the money goes back through Stripe; one paid by a payment link or in cash is marked as refunded instead, which records it without moving money.

faq.question: Does Event Schedule support post-event surveys?
faq.answer: Yes, on the Pro plan. After an event, attendees are emailed a request for a star rating and a comment (on eventschedule.com the email goes out through your own email settings), and the results stay with that event. Event polls, also Pro, put a quick question with up to ten answers on the event page. What it does not have is SurveyMonkey-style branching logic, so a long research survey still belongs in a survey tool.

faq.question: Does Event Schedule support attendee limits and waitlists?
faq.answer: Yes. Set capacity limits per ticket type, and when an event sells out, people can join a waitlist and get notified if spots open up. The RSVP waitlist is free; the ticket waitlist is on the Pro plan. For an event that is not on sale yet, the free interest list takes just an email address and says when tickets go on sale.

faq.question: Can I collect custom information from attendees?
faq.answer: Yes. Pro plan includes custom fields on ticket forms so you can collect any information you need during registration. The data is connected to attendee records and available for export.

faq.question: Can people register interest before tickets go on sale?
faq.answer: Yes, free on every plan. On an event that is not selling yet, visitors leave just an email address, with no account and no survey. They hear when tickets go on sale, if the event is cancelled, and shortly before it starts, plus any notice you choose to send if the date or venue changes, and every email has a one-click unsubscribe. The event editor shows you how many people are waiting.

faq.question: How much does QR code ticketing cost?
faq.answer: Nothing, to start. The free plan sells up to 25 paid tickets a month per schedule, each with its own QR code, and scanning them at the door is not gated at all. faq.question: How does the QR check-in system work?

faq.question: Can I use QR check-in without selling tickets?

faq.question: Do I need special hardware to scan QR codes?
faq.answer: No. Any smartphone with a web browser can scan tickets. Open the check-in page on your phone, point it at the QR code, and the attendee is checked in instantly. No app download required.

faq.question: Can attendees keep their ticket in Google Wallet?
faq.answer: Yes, on installs where Google Wallet is set up, and on every plan. The ticket page, the order page and the confirmation email carry an Add to Google Wallet button, and the pass shows the same QR code, so it scans at the door like the emailed ticket. Free registrations get a pass too.

faq.question: Is Event Schedule a good Notion alternative for event planning?
faq.answer: Yes, for the event management side. Event Schedule handles everything Notion cannot: public event pages, ticket sales, attendee management, Google Calendar sync, and newsletters. You may still use Notion for internal project notes, but Event Schedule replaces it for audience-facing event work.

faq.question: Is Event Schedule free like Notion?
faq.answer: Yes. The free plan includes unlimited events, public event pages, Google Calendar sync, newsletters and event graphics, and selling is free too, 25 paid tickets a month at zero platform fees. The Pro plan at $5/month removes that ceiling and adds the live check-in dashboard. One difference worth knowing before you move a team off Notion: a free schedule is a single account, and multiple team members, up to five, are an Enterprise feature.

faq.question: Does Event Schedule support team collaboration like Notion?
faq.answer: Yes, on the Enterprise plan, which carries up to five team members. An admin runs the schedule day to day and sees its ticket sales, and a viewer is read-only but can scan tickets at the door. Unlike Notion, collaboration is purpose-built for event management with tools like shared schedules, sub-schedules, and delegated event editing.

faq.question: Is Event Schedule easier to set up than a Notion event database?
faq.answer: Yes. Create a schedule in under a minute with no databases, templates, or formulas to configure. Add events with AI import or manual entry and you have a public event page with ticketing immediately. No workspace setup needed.

faq.question: Can I use Event Schedule alongside Notion?
faq.answer: Yes. Many organizers use Notion for internal project planning and Event Schedule for the audience-facing side: public event pages, ticket sales, newsletters, and attendee management. On Pro, the REST API can also connect Event Schedule data with your Notion workflows.

faq.question: Can I reuse an event as a template, the way I would in Notion?
faq.answer: Yes, on Pro. Save any event as a template and start new events from it on the Templates tab, with its details already filled in.
